title: Fix three bugs in Rust string utilities: reverse, word count, and capitalize
description: Dirty-cleanup Rust task: three string functions have obvious logic bugs. All tests are written correctly; the implementations must be fixed to make them pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Fix three bugs in src/lib.rs. All 9 tests must pass after your fixes.

Bug 1 — reverse_string:
  Current: s.to_string()  (returns unchanged)
  Fix: collect chars in reverse order: s.chars().rev().collect()

Bug 2 — count_words:
  Current: s.len()  (counts bytes, not words)
  Fix: s.split_whitespace().count()

Bug 3 — capitalize:
  Current: s.to_uppercase()  (uppercases entire string)
  Fix: uppercase only the first char; leave the rest unchanged
  Hint: use s.chars(), take the first with .next(), uppercase it, then append the remainder with chars.as_str()

Run: cargo test
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to check the current state. Walk me through what bugs you found and fixed. If any tests are still failing, show me the errors and fix them.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — if any are still red, fix them now.
